newsitem.title: USA: NYSE March 24-27 program trading averages 18.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE March 24-27 program trading averages 18.4 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading during March 24-27 amounted to 18.4 percent of NYSE average daily volume of 480.3 million shares, or 88.6 million shares a day.

The NYSE's program-trading report includes profiles of program trading whenever the Dow Jones Industrial Average moves 50 points or more in a single direction during any one-hour period. During March 24-27, there were four such periods.
Of the total average daily volume, buy programs accounted for 47.1 million shares daily and sell programs accounted for 41.5 million shares daily on average.
In all markets, program trading averaged 114.1 million shares a day during March 24-27.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, BNP Securities, Natwest, Goldman Sachs, Susquehanna Brokerage and Morgan Stanley each execute all or most of their program activity for customers, as agent or facilitator.

During March 24-27, 25 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage, while 0.7 percent involved derivative product-related strategies. All other types of portfolio-trading strategies combined accounted for 74.3 percent.
Program trading enompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more, the exchange said.
